counterfactual_missing_items: the absence of pathological enhancement of the pons
no raw span showing response to plasmapheresis
no biopsy/autopsy or CSF-specific demyelinating/infectious marker in the raw evidence
decisive_items: These findings were thought to represent an acute demyelinating process
progressive enlargement of the bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle
increased signaling of the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete supplied composite: as the completion of R3, it carries the explicit acute demyelinating process/encephalopathy diagnosis and adds the independently raw-supported hydrocephalus and mass-effect complication. R3 is runner-up because it captures the core diagnosis but omits the complication; its multiple demyelinating phrases are correlated restatements and were discounted accordingly. R1 explains only the later mass-effect via a disjunctive low-grade glioma mention while ignoring the multifocal demyelinating MRI. R6 is undermined by absent pontine enhancement, R2 lacks optic neuritis or NMO-specific raw support, and R4 has no raw support spans. Generator assessments were not counted as evidence.

rejected.why: Only late disjunctive mention of low-grade glioma plus mass effect; cannot explain the early multifocal demyelinating MRI or the explicit acute demyelinating encephalopathy diagnosis.
Shares nonspecific demyelinating raw evidence but is contradicted by the absence of pathological enhancement of the pons and lacks the hydrocephalus/mass-effect complication.
Cervical cord and brainstem MRI signal is compatible, but raw evidence lacks optic neuritis and any NMO-specific finding to compete with the labelled ADEM diagnosis.
No raw support spans are supplied; the suspicion of infectious encephalitis is a nonliteral/generator assessment rather than direct raw diagnostic evidence.
